solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Turned up with barge: river an easy challenge

indicators.note: turned over, the little word that follows is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to barge is to push roughly, to shove

explanation.surface: A boat flipped over when rammed by a barge, and the river turned out to be no great test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like part of the boating scene but reverses the little word after it; the colon hides where the definition begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is informal for a task or opponent beaten with no real effort.

clue.text: Old man, unusually spry, snatching University manuscript from long ago

parts.note: pa is informal for father, one's old man

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing and holding, so the scramble takes the university letter inside
unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A sprightly father unusually grabs an ancient university document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes PYRS of SPRY, and 'snatching' sets U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus was the writing material of ancient Egypt, and a document written on it is also called one.

clue.text: No US city's backing artistic gathering

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, plus the S from the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An American city declines to support an arts event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads like support, but it reverses the letters; the apostrophe S of 'city's' is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is an elegant gathering of writers and artists in a host's home, as in old Paris.

clue.text: Panting, about to engage in towelling oneself down?

indicators.note: engage in means to enter into, so the short word goes inside

parts.note: drying off with a towel is what you do when out of the bath
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone gasping as they briskly dry themselves after a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to engage in' sets the word for 'about' inside the bath phrase; the question mark admits that towelling down is only one sign of being out of the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of breath means gasping for air after effort, the same state as panting.

clue.text: Article is elevated in cathedral without difficulty

indicators.note: the article and lifted word go inside the cathedral city

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: elevated means lifted up, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is put on a high shelf in the cathedral with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns IS into SI; A + SI goes 'in' ELY, a small cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means with no trouble at all, an adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Gift paper maybe will revolutionise any present at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset of each of the four words before it, so only their opening letters are wanted

explanation.surface: Fancy wrapping paper promises to transform any gift it covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' takes the first letters of 'will revolutionise any present'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrap is the decorative paper used to cover presents, as in gift wrap; 'maybe' marks it as one kind.

clue.text: Lacking energy and listing

definitions.meaning: a ... is a summary list of points

explanation.surface: Someone tired and leaning over to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling run-down means exhausted, while a rundown is a brief itemised account.

clue.text: Request time to make feature of dress

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request

explanation.surface: Asking for more time to sew a dress detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn into a skirt or dress, so it is one of its design elements.

clue.text: Trial episode: one's gripped by storyline

indicators.note: one is held inside by the storyline word, so it goes within it

parts.note: a storyline is a plot
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A TV producer says the first trial show hooks a viewer with its story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's gripped by' reads as 'one is gripped by': I goes inside PLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is the test episode a network makes before commissioning a whole television series.

clue.text: Peace in the time following admitting the French

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the French article goes inside

parts.note: since means in the time following, as in 'since the war'
le is the French masculine 'the'

explanation.surface: Peace has reigned in the years after France was let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals insertion; 'in' is only a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is a state of quiet, and peace often means calm and freedom from noise.

clue.text: Allege beauty mostly misrepresented in sports ranking

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented falsely, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not all of it, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone falsely claims a beauty contest ranks as a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BEAUTY to BEAUT; 'misrepresented' scrambles ALLEGE BEAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A league table lists teams in order of points, the standing in a sports competition.

clue.text: I will escape financial disaster in banking crisis?

indicators.note: if I will escape, that letter gets out of the word that follows

parts.note: ruin is complete financial collapse

explanation.surface: Someone vows to dodge bankruptcy during a banking meltdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will escape' drops the I from RUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A run on a bank is when depositors all rush to withdraw at once; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Amateur's debut in autumn fight? That'll make you laugh

indicators.note: the amateur's first letter sits inside the pair of words for autumn and fight

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
a bout is a boxing match or fight

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A novice's first autumn boxing contest is promised to be a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debut' takes the amateur's first letter and 'in' sets it inside; 'autumn' as FALL is the American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall about is British slang for laughing helplessly; the clue's last sentence describes something that makes you do it.

clue.text: Odds at this point offering a round figure

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price, the odds at the off
here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: A bookmaker offers odds that come out as a nice even number.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price in horse racing, is the odds quoted when the race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is the perfectly round solid shape of geometry, such as a ball.

clue.text: Swindler hurtles around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A conman dashes all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is a con artist who tricks people out of money.

clue.text: Direct pleasure offered by King's mistress mostly

parts.note: fun is enjoyment or pleasure

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: Instructions on giving a royal mistress enjoyment, as in a Restoration comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was an actress and famous mistress of Charles II; 'mostly' cuts NELL to NEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To funnel something is to channel or steer it towards a place, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Extended line, English, for you in the Bible?

parts.note: thy is the archaic form for 'your', found in the King James Bible

explanation.surface: An extended line in English used for the second person in Scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly THY means 'your', the old possessive used in the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthy means long and drawn out, as an extended speech is.

clue.text: Arab leader accepting last list of discussion items

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for last goes inside

parts.note: an aga is a Muslim commander or chief
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: A sheikh agrees to the final schedule for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab leader' looks like a first-letter pick, but here it is a title for a chief; 'accepting' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the written list of matters to be dealt with at a meeting.

clue.text: Attack expression of humour with tons going wrong outside

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes around the outside of the expression of humour
going wrong means the letters fall into disorder and are rearranged

parts.note: a laugh expresses amusement

explanation.surface: A comic's joke falls badly flat with tons of weight, and becomes an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' turns TONS into ONST, which goes 'outside' LAUGH: ONS + LAUGH + T.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, overwhelming assault, so it is a noun synonym for attack.

clue.text: Tell British to abandon frontier

indicators.note: abandon means leave behind, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a border is a frontier between countries

explanation.surface: Instruct the British to give up guarding the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To order someone is to command them, as in telling them what to do.

clue.text: Little point in security number?

definitions.meaning: a ... has a tiny sharp point
a personal identification number, guarding a bank card

explanation.surface: Is there any point to the little security code on my card?
explanation.definitionFit: A pin is a small pointed fastener, and the acronym names the secret code for cards.

clue.text: Scotsman in Post Office to get instrument

indicators.note: the Scotsman goes inside the abbreviation for Post Office

parts.note: Ian is a common Scottish man's name, standard in crosswords

explanation.surface: A Scot goes to the post office to collect a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is a keyboard musical instrument with hammers striking strings.

clue.text: Marine creature in hold at sea retains power

indicators.note: retains means keeps within, so the power letter sits inside the scramble
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A sea creature trapped in a ship's hold keeps its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns IN HOLD into DOLHIN, which 'retains' P.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a sea mammal, so it is one example of a creature living in the ocean.

clue.text: Prow of boat to survive storm

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure

explanation.surface: The front of a boat must hold up through a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a violent gust of wind, and a storm is a spell of such wild weather.

clue.text: Runs are hard to come by

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket observation: scoring runs is difficult today.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is scarce and seldom found, so it is difficult to obtain.

clue.text: Chartered accountant, for example, participating in Conservative group

indicators.note: taking part in means going within, so the example letters sit inside

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An accountant, say, takes part in a Conservative party committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'participating in' places only the 'for example' abbreviation inside the party word; the accountant stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class of things sharing features, which is another word for a group.
